## 50b66a854306

**Classification: suspected shortcut reproduced on the easy generated domain; source left unchanged.**

I checked all five canonical inputs with the target validator, 300 final-source samples in each band (seed 918273, sample indices 0–299), and 64 generated easy inputs through the supported Racket apply command. All canonical inputs pass `self_check`.

The rival predicts a positive off-diagonal relation only for opposite-chirality/reflection-equivalent shapes, not for shapes related only by rotation; diagonal entries remain positive. It matches **300/300 easy** Python-rule draws, but only **200/300 medium** and **200/300 hard** draws. It matches **64/64 actual Racket outputs** on retained generated easy inputs (`checks/audit/50b66a854306/generated_comparison.json`). It fails four of five canonical pairs. Canonical pair 0 is retained as a supported Racket counterexample in `checks/audit/50b66a854306/counterexample.json`; the input passes the target validator and its documented general domain.

This does not prove the full curriculum is wrong: medium and hard refute the rival in one third of the sampled draws. It does show that easy-band lessons can teach a stable incomplete symmetry concept if sampled alone, and the current declared tests do not force a rotation-only positive example. Aggregate source-bound evidence is in `checks/audit/probe_results.json`. Generator SHA-256 remained `56012755f29c25630bcd8c131f46e73902fbea95021d2a302449620583217672`; executed rule hash was `0b773d88a636`.
